idea-plugin.name: JS Console
idea-plugin.description:
A Chrome DevTools–style console for JavaScript and TypeScript projects, running on Bun. Try code against your project without leaving WebStorm.

  • The file open in the editor is the console's context: call its functions, classes and variables by name, exported or not, with no imports.
  • Files run only when the console first uses them; switching editor tabs never executes code.
  • Variables persist between commands; const, let and class can be redeclared while you iterate, as in DevTools.
  • Top-level await, import statements, JavaScript highlighting, completion and command history.
  • Pending promises never block the console; uncaught errors are printed, never fatal.
  • Keep extra files in context with Add File to JS Console or Add Symbol to JS Console.
  • Optional debugger: breakpoints stop console calls, and while any JavaScript program you debug is paused, the console evaluates in the selected stack frame.

Requires Bun 1.4 or newer. Open View | Tool Windows | JS Console.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.2.0

  • Evaluates in the paused frame of any JavaScript program you debug.
  • Console output appears in order with command results.
  • Context files are no longer executed when you switch editor tabs.
  • Non-exported top-level declarations are available by name.
  • Awaited commands no longer block the console; a busy JavaScript thread is reported.
  • Uncaught errors no longer stop the runtime; console and project code share one realm.
  • Debugger toggle in the tool window; Restart also ends processes started from the console.
